currentContext.strengths: Described as the only Indian player with a single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility, producing key intermediates such as sponge iron, slabs and HR coils in-house|One of the few domestic producers of narrow-width hot rolled coils through a secondary steelmaking route (DRI plus induction furnace), which reduces capital expenditure in pipe manufacturing and dependence on external HR coil suppliers|Among a limited number of manufacturers in India producing stainless steel blooms/slabs through the Argon Oxygen Decarburization (AOD) process, described as cost-effective|Ladle Refining Furnace capability allows alloy steel production through the induction furnace route, including Corten steel pipes|Advanced Non-Ox technology for pre-galvanized coils and pipes uses significantly less zinc, improving cost efficiency without compromising quality|Captive WHRB and AFBC power plants utilise waste heat and by-products such as dolochar for power generation, the WHRB requiring no additional fuel|Strategic location in Raipur, Chhattisgarh close to coal and high-grade iron ore, with iron ore sourced from a Navratna public sector enterprise and coal largely from a subsidiary of India's largest coal producer situated within 250 kms of the facilities|Dealer-distributor network across 15 states and one Union Territory with over 47 distributors and more than 1,000 dealers, supporting stable double-digit operating margins|Long-term ratings reaffirmed during FY 2025-26 at CARE A (Stable) and ACUITE A (Stable), with short-term ratings maintained at CARE A1 and ACUITE A1
currentContext.strategies: Vision 2030 is presented as an institutional growth framework rather than a project list, aligning capital allocation, manufacturing expansion, product diversification, operational excellence and financial prudence around a common long-term objective.|Growth is sequenced in planned phases so that each investment is commissioned, stabilised and generating returns before the next phase begins, preserving balance sheet integrity and financial flexibility.|Vision 2030 is to be funded with prioritised investment sequencing, conservative leverage and internal accrual-based funding, with the quantum of investment envisaged substantially higher than the capital deployed over the growth journey to date.|Deliberate positioning in structural tubes, coated products and stainless steel - faster-growing, higher-value segments - rather than commodity steel, and building capabilities ahead of anticipated demand rather than reacting to it.|Three pillars of competitive strength: specialisation in stainless steel, coated and specialised steel products; full backward integration at a single location; and energy security through captive power generation.|Integration as a competitive advantage: deepen backward integration to strengthen supply-chain control and reduce input-cost volatility, and expand captive power generation to enhance energy security.|Expand manufacturing scale: leapfrog production capacity, leverage available infrastructure, and increase finished steel capacity from 0.62 MMTPA to 2.03 MMTPA.|Enhance value: increase stainless steel, coated steel and specialised steel product offerings, raise the share of value-added steel in the revenue mix, and enhance overall blended margins.|Build a national steel brand: strengthen visibility around the 'Sab Sambhv Hai' campaign, build recognition through IPL partnerships, airport branding and digital engagement, and expand co-branding partnerships with stainless steel pipe manufacturers.|Wider and deeper distribution footprint: deepen presence in high-growth domestic markets, establish an 'always around the corner' reputation, and help enhance the working capital efficiency of trade partners.|Target a through-cycle franchise: protect and preserve market share in downcycles via margin resilience and cash-flow protection, and scale and accelerate in upcycles via faster response to demand and stronger pricing power, across ERW pipes, stainless steel coils and coated steel products.
currentContext.expansion: The Company has grown by successive brownfield capacity additions at its Raipur, Chhattisgarh complex. Its key-milestones timeline records commencement of sponge iron manufacture in 2018 at 60,000 MTPA, expansion of sponge iron to 90,000 MTPA in 2019, commissioning of a 15 MW captive power plant (6 MW WHRB plus 9 MW AFBC) together with the start of blooms/slabs production at 120,000 MTPA in 2020, expansion of blooms/slabs to 150,000 MTPA and entry into hot rolled coils at 150,000 MTPA in 2022, an increase of blooms/slabs to 317,000 MTPA plus the start of Galvanized Iron (GI) pipe production and commissioning of a 132 kVA power line in 2023, and in 2024 sponge iron to 105,000 MTPA, blooms/slabs to 231,000 MTPA, HR coils to 350,000 MTPA and the start of ERW pipe manufacture at an initial 150,000 MTPA subsequently expanded to 250,000 MTPA. In 2025 sponge iron reached 280,000 MTPA, HR coils 390,000 MTPA and ERW pipes and structural tubes 350,000 MTPA, the captive power plant was enhanced to 25 MW (16 MW WHRB and 9 MW AFBC), the Company gained the capability to manufacture stainless steel blooms/slabs and stainless steel HR coils (60,000 MTPA) alongside stainless steel cold rolled coils (58,000 MTPA), and it commenced GP coils and GP pipes at 58,000 MTPA and 100,000 MTPA respectively. In 2026 the Company raised H440 crore and listed on the Indian stock exchanges; pre-galvanized (GP) coil installed capacity doubled from 58,000 MTPA to 1,16,000 MTPA; greenfield project execution started at Kesda; the Company signed an MoU with the Ministry of Steel under the PLI Scheme 1.2 for manufacturing stainless steel CR coils; and it undertook a brownfield capacity expansion from 58,000 MTPA to 116,000 MTPA for stainless steel (the report states this expansion range for stainless steel as well as for GP coils, and the two statements are not reconciled in the text supplied). Looking forward, the Directors' Report records that the Board, in its meeting held on May 09, 2026, approved a capex investment of H2,000.00 million to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route, adding 150,000 MTPA of production capacity at the existing Sarora unit, and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Village Sarora Unit-III, Tehsil-Tilda, Dist-Raipur, Chhattisgarh; no commissioning date is stated for either. Revenue growth during FY 2025-26 is attributed in part to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel.
currentContext.mdna: India remains in the early stages of industrialisation, with per capita steel consumption of around 104 kilograms - less than half the global average - a gap management expects to narrow steadily over the coming decades, creating one of the world's longest visible steel demand runways.|Domestic steel demand is described as moving towards 190-230 million tonnes by 2030, with the National Steel Policy targeting 300 MTPA steelmaking capacity.|Specialised and value-added steel products are expected to grow faster than commodity steel; management argues value addition, integration and operational excellence, rather than manufacturing scale alone, will define competitiveness.|Structural tubes and stainless steel continue to replace conventional materials across construction, water infrastructure, engineering and industrial applications on superior strength-to-weight ratio and efficiency.|Stainless steel and coated products are seeing rising demand across automotive, railways, renewable energy, process industries and precision engineering on durability, corrosion resistance and life-cycle endurance.|Mix is the key margin lever: value-added products contributed 92.66% of total revenue during FY 2025-26 (82.86% in FY 2024-25 and 80.05% in FY 2023-24), and the increasing contribution of value-added products enhanced blended realisations, enabling revenue growth to outpace volume growth.|The commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel significantly expanded the addressable market while increasing availability of higher-value products.|Highest-ever sales volume of 396,731 MT was achieved through expanding customer reach, improved production efficiencies and growing demand for value-added products.|High capacity utilisation across key stainless steel facilities is cited as reflecting growing customer acceptance and as providing the rationale for the next phase of capacity expansion.|A self-reinforcing cycle is described whereby demand growth raises the value-added share, higher value addition enhances profitability, and stronger profitability generates internal cash flows to fund the next phase of expansion, with backward integration retaining a greater proportion of earnings within the Company.|Interest coverage improved to 5.43x in FY 2025-26 from 2.65x in FY 2024-25, supported by higher operating earnings and lower finance costs following the reduction in borrowings after the IPO.

risks.risk: Single-location geographic concentration of all manufacturing
risks.note: The Sarora (Tilda) integrated facility, the Kuthrel facility and the Kesda greenfield land are all stated to lie within a 10-kilometre radius of the principal manufacturing unit in Chhattisgarh, and the Company presents itself as a fully integrated, single-location platform. Any local disruption affecting that one cluster would affect the entire value chain from sponge iron to finished pipes at once. This bundle does not contain a Risks and Concerns section; the risk is read off the disclosed footprint.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the newly approved expansion, with no stated commissioning timeline
risks.note: The Directors' Report records Board approval on May 09, 2026 of a H2,000.00 million capex to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route by 150,000 MTPA at the existing Sarora unit and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Sarora Unit-III. No completion or commissioning date is stated for either element, so progress cannot be tracked against a company-stated deadline.

risks.risk: Growth funded by retained earnings rather than distribution
risks.note: In view of ongoing expansion plans and the requirement to conserve resources for funding growth initiatives, the Board did not recommend any dividend for the year ended March 31, 2026 and decided to retain the entire profit for FY2025-26 in the statement of profit and loss. Shareholder returns are therefore wholly dependent on the expansion programme delivering.

risks.risk: Dependence on third parties for contracted power arrangements
risks.note: The Share Purchase Agreement relating to the Company's investment in CleanMax Opia Private Limited was terminated because CMOPL could not acquire the requisite land and obtain Stage II connectivity approval under the Energy Supply Agreement, and the Company divested its entire shareholding of 2,600 equity shares, with CMOPL ceasing to be an associate from May 30, 2025. This is a realised instance of a contracted external power arrangement failing on approvals.

risks.risk: Dependence on the ramp-up of recently commissioned capacity
risks.note: Both the Directors' Report and the corporate overview attribute FY 2025-26 revenue growth to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel and to the resulting shift in product mix. Earnings momentum is therefore tied to sustaining utilisation and market acceptance at facilities that have only recently started up.

risks.risk: Reliance on a large contract workforce alongside permanent employees
risks.note: As of March 31, 2026 the Company employed 2,303 permanent employees and 1,643 contract workers. The report states the workforce remains non-unionised and industrial relations were stable without significant labour-related disruptions, but roughly two-fifths of the workforce is engaged on a contract basis.

risks.risk: Concentration of leadership in the founding family
risks.note: The Company states it is led by promoters Brijlal Goyal, Suresh Kumar Goyal and Vikas Kumar Goyal, who collectively possess over 50 years of steel manufacturing experience, with the leadership team strengthened by Bhavesh Khetan as Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer. Strategic direction and execution rest on a small, related group of individuals.

risks.risk: Short track record as a listed company
risks.note: FY 2025-26 was the Company's first full financial year as a listed entity following its IPO and listing on NSE and BSE, so its disclosure, governance and capital-market track record is limited to a single completed year.

one-line thesis: Sambhv Steel delivered a landmark Q4FY26 with PAT doubling to INR 56 Cr and EBITDA/ton peaking at INR 9,500 driven by low-cost raw material inventory and strong realizations. The company is aggressively expanding capacity toward a 2 Mn ton target by 2030, leveraging PLI incentives and captive power to sustain margins despite rising input costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 685 Cr (+38% YoY); EBITDA: INR 92 Cr (+91% YoY), Margin 13% (vs ~11% FY26 avg); PAT: INR 56 Cr (>100% YoY), Normalized for one-off inventory gains from low-cost Q3 procurement; Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but demand cited as robust across infrastructure; Net Debt: Peak long-term debt guided at INR 800 Cr + INR 200-300 Cr WC post-capex.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Volume growth 10-15% in FY27; Margin: EBITDA/ton INR 7,500-8,000 sustainable in FY27 (Q4 peak of 9,500 due to inventory lag); Order Inflow: Strong demand from solar, warehousing, railways; Capex/Commissioning: Kesda Phase 1 (3.6 L ton SS) by Q4FY27; Brownfield SS debottlenecking (1.16 L ton) immediate.
order book & pipeline: Management cites strong demand visibility from government capex (railways, metros, airports, solar 500GW target) but does not disclose a specific numeric order book value; utilization targets imply healthy fill-rates (SS 60-65%, MS 65-70%, GP 80-90%).
segment / subsidiary detail: Carbon Steel: ERW pipes/tubes, GP pipes/coils; Stainless Steel: CR coils (200/300 series), expanding to 400 series; Value-add: Co-branding MOUs (10 live) for pipe manufacturing.
growth verticals / optionality: 2 Mn ton finished steel capacity by 2030 (10 L ton MS pipes, 3 L ton coated, 7 L ton SS); Greenfield Kesda project (Phase 1: 3.6 L ton SS); Potential seamless pipe entry under PLI 1.2 pending approvals.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA/ton INR 9,500 inflated by Q3 low-cost raw material (iron ore/coal) usage; FY27 guidance INR 7,500-8,000/ton; Power cost savings of INR 60-70 Cr expected from new captive plants; Raw material pass-through estimated at 50-60% of realization hikes.
capex / expansion: Total identified capex INR 1.13k Cr (INR 930 Cr Kesda Phase 1 + INR 200 Cr operational efficiency/power/DFT); Funding: INR 675 Cr term loan for Kesda, balance internal accruals/debt; Additional INR 300-400 Cr potential capex by FY28 for undefined Phase 2/3.
capital allocation: Debt prudence policy: Long-term debt <1.5x Net Worth and <1.5x Forward EBITDA; INR 100 Cr parked in liquid mutual funds (current investments); Focus on internal accruals for incremental efficiency capex.
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (iron ore/coal); Execution risk on 2 Mn ton expansion; Working capital cycle elongation (guided to 25-30 days) as SS mix increases; Geopolitical impacts on energy/logistics (mitigated by captive power/LNG).
management quality / tone: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'Sambhv hai, toh sab sambhv hai' (If Sambhv exists, everything is possible); Prudent on debt but aggressive on volume/market share targets (10-12% share in MS/SS by 2030).
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory accounting method (WIP valued at cost) neutralizes stock profit/loss volatility; DFT technology reduces size-changeover time from 3-4 hours to near-instant, boosting effective capacity by 10-12k ton/month per machine; PLI incentive capped at ~INR 200 Cr or tonnage, providing a 13-15% revenue boost on eligible thin-gauge production.

hero.oneLiner: Sambhv Steel Tubes is a domestic manufacturer of ERW pipes, galvanized products and stainless steel coils, operating what it describes as the only single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility in India.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sambhv Steel Tubes is a domestic manufacturer of ERW pipes, galvanized products and stainless steel coils, operating what it describes as the only single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures structural tubes and stainless steel products from two backward-integrated facilities in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, addressing the value chain from iron ore through sponge iron, blooms/slabs and HR coils to finished ERW black pipes, pre-galvanized coils and pipes, and stainless steel HRAP and CR coils. Products go into infrastructure, industrial, automotive, agricultural and residential applications. Sales are made largely through a distributor network of over 47 distributors serving more than 1,000 dealers, retailers and fabricators, with close engagement of EPC contractors, OEMs, infrastructure developers and fabricators.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Management cites strong demand visibility from government capex (railways, metros, airports, solar 500GW target) but does not disclose a specific numeric order book value; utilization targets imply healthy fill-rates (SS 60-65%, MS 65-70%, GP 80-90%).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Volume growth 10-15% in FY27; Margin: EBITDA/ton INR 7,500-8,000 sustainable in FY27 (Q4 peak of 9,500 due to inventory lag); Order Inflow: Strong demand from solar, warehousing, railways; Capex/Commissioning: Kesda Phase 1 (3.6 L ton SS) by Q4FY27; Brownfield SS debottlenecking (1.16 L ton) immediate.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 2 Mn ton finished steel capacity by 2030 (10 L ton MS pipes, 3 L ton coated, 7 L ton SS); Greenfield Kesda project (Phase 1: 3.6 L ton SS); Potential seamless pipe entry under PLI 1.2 pending approvals.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains in the early stages of industrialisation, with per capita steel consumption of around 104 kilograms - less than half the global average - a gap management expects to narrow steadily over the coming decades, creating one of the world's longest visible steel demand runways.
- Domestic steel demand is described as moving towards 190-230 million tonnes by 2030, with the National Steel Policy targeting 300 MTPA steelmaking capacity.
- Specialised and value-added steel products are expected to grow faster than commodity steel; management argues value addition, integration and operational excellence, rather than manufacturing scale alone, will define competitiveness.
- Structural tubes and stainless steel continue to replace conventional materials across construction, water infrastructure, engineering and industrial applications on superior strength-to-weight ratio and efficiency.
- Stainless steel and coated products are seeing rising demand across automotive, railways, renewable energy, process industries and precision engineering on durability, corrosion resistance and life-cycle endurance.
- Mix is the key margin lever: value-added products contributed 92.66% of total revenue during FY 2025-26 (82.86% in FY 2024-25 and 80.05% in FY 2023-24), and the increasing contribution of value-added products enhanced blended realisations, enabling revenue growth to outpace volume growth.
- The commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel significantly expanded the addressable market while increasing availability of higher-value products.
- Highest-ever sales volume of 396,731 MT was achieved through expanding customer reach, improved production efficiencies and growing demand for value-added products.
- High capacity utilisation across key stainless steel facilities is cited as reflecting growing customer acceptance and as providing the rationale for the next phase of capacity expansion.
- A self-reinforcing cycle is described whereby demand growth raises the value-added share, higher value addition enhances profitability, and stronger profitability generates internal cash flows to fund the next phase of expansion, with backward integration retaining a greater proportion of earnings within the Company.
- Interest coverage improved to 5.43x in FY 2025-26 from 2.65x in FY 2024-25, supported by higher operating earnings and lower finance costs following the reduction in borrowings after the IPO.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA/ton INR 9,500 inflated by Q3 low-cost raw material (iron ore/coal) usage; FY27 guidance INR 7,500-8,000/ton; Power cost savings of INR 60-70 Cr expected from new captive plants; Raw material pass-through estimated at 50-60% of realization hikes.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt prudence policy: Long-term debt <1.5x Net Worth and <1.5x Forward EBITDA; INR 100 Cr parked in liquid mutual funds (current investments); Focus on internal accruals for incremental efficiency capex.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has grown by successive brownfield capacity additions at its Raipur, Chhattisgarh complex. Its key-milestones timeline records commencement of sponge iron manufacture in 2018 at 60,000 MTPA, expansion of sponge iron to 90,000 MTPA in 2019, commissioning of a 15 MW captive power plant (6 MW WHRB plus 9 MW AFBC) together with the start of blooms/slabs production at 120,000 MTPA in 2020, expansion of blooms/slabs to 150,000 MTPA and entry into hot rolled coils at 150,000 MTPA in 2022, an increase of blooms/slabs to 317,000 MTPA plus the start of Galvanized Iron (GI) pipe production and commissioning of a 132 kVA power line in 2023, and in 2024 sponge iron to 105,000 MTPA, blooms/slabs to 231,000 MTPA, HR coils to 350,000 MTPA and the start of ERW pipe manufacture at an initial 150,000 MTPA subsequently expanded to 250,000 MTPA. In 2025 sponge iron reached 280,000 MTPA, HR coils 390,000 MTPA and ERW pipes and structural tubes 350,000 MTPA, the captive power plant was enhanced to 25 MW (16 MW WHRB and 9 MW AFBC), the Company gained the capability to manufacture stainless steel blooms/slabs and stainless steel HR coils (60,000 MTPA) alongside stainless steel cold rolled coils (58,000 MTPA), and it commenced GP coils and GP pipes at 58,000 MTPA and 100,000 MTPA respectively. In 2026 the Company raised H440 crore and listed on the Indian stock exchanges; pre-galvanized (GP) coil installed capacity doubled from 58,000 MTPA to 1,16,000 MTPA; greenfield project execution started at Kesda; the Company signed an MoU with the Ministry of Steel under the PLI Scheme 1.2 for manufacturing stainless steel CR coils; and it undertook a brownfield capacity expansion from 58,000 MTPA to 116,000 MTPA for stainless steel (the report states this expansion range for stainless steel as well as for GP coils, and the two statements are not reconciled in the text supplied). Looking forward, the Directors' Report records that the Board, in its meeting held on May 09, 2026, approved a capex investment of H2,000.00 million to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route, adding 150,000 MTPA of production capacity at the existing Sarora unit, and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Village Sarora Unit-III, Tehsil-Tilda, Dist-Raipur, Chhattisgarh; no commissioning date is stated for either. Revenue growth during FY 2025-26 is attributed in part to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'Sambhv hai, toh sab sambhv hai' (If Sambhv exists, everything is possible); Prudent on debt but aggressive on volume/market share targets (10-12% share in MS/SS by 2030).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Described as the only Indian player with a single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility, producing key intermediates such as sponge iron, slabs and HR coils in-house
- One of the few domestic producers of narrow-width hot rolled coils through a secondary steelmaking route (DRI plus induction furnace), which reduces capital expenditure in pipe manufacturing and dependence on external HR coil suppliers
- Among a limited number of manufacturers in India producing stainless steel blooms/slabs through the Argon Oxygen Decarburization (AOD) process, described as cost-effective
- Ladle Refining Furnace capability allows alloy steel production through the induction furnace route, including Corten steel pipes
- Advanced Non-Ox technology for pre-galvanized coils and pipes uses significantly less zinc, improving cost efficiency without compromising quality
- Captive WHRB and AFBC power plants utilise waste heat and by-products such as dolochar for power generation, the WHRB requiring no additional fuel
- Strategic location in Raipur, Chhattisgarh close to coal and high-grade iron ore, with iron ore sourced from a Navratna public sector enterprise and coal largely from a subsidiary of India's largest coal producer situated within 250 kms of the facilities
- Dealer-distributor network across 15 states and one Union Territory with over 47 distributors and more than 1,000 dealers, supporting stable double-digit operating margins
- Long-term ratings reaffirmed during FY 2025-26 at CARE A (Stable) and ACUITE A (Stable), with short-term ratings maintained at CARE A1 and ACUITE A1

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material price volatility (iron ore/coal); Execution risk on 2 Mn ton expansion; Working capital cycle elongation (guided to 25-30 days) as SS mix increases; Geopolitical impacts on energy/logistics (mitigated by captive power/LNG).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory accounting method (WIP valued at cost) neutralizes stock profit/loss volatility; DFT technology reduces size-changeover time from 3-4 hours to near-instant, boosting effective capacity by 10-12k ton/month per machine; PLI incentive capped at ~INR 200 Cr or tonnage, providing a 13-15% revenue boost on eligible thin-gauge production.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Vision 2030 is presented as an institutional growth framework rather than a project list, aligning capital allocation, manufacturing expansion, product diversification, operational excellence and financial prudence around a common long-term objective.
- Growth is sequenced in planned phases so that each investment is commissioned, stabilised and generating returns before the next phase begins, preserving balance sheet integrity and financial flexibility.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Execution status] The Kesda project is tracked work-package by work-package: 132KV line and sub-station ongoing (target Q4FY27), civil work for the technological structure ~90% (power plant), ~30% (steel melting shop), ~80% (hot rolling mill) and ~40% (Kuthrel Unit-II cold rolling mill), with key machinery ordering completed in Q4FY26 across all divisions and testing/commissioning targeted Q4FY27; site photographs are dated July 26, 2026.
- [Standalone scope] Every financial figure in the deck is labelled standalone, yet the cash flow statement shows an investment in subsidiary of INR 652 Million (FY25), a loan given to subsidiary of INR 8 Million and repayment of loan from subsidiary of INR 273 Million (FY26) - so subsidiary economics are outside the presented numbers.
- [Brand spend] Entered IPL branding through cricket bat sponsorship of multiple players including Prabhsimran Singh and Mukul Choudhary, alongside electronic/outdoor/digital/print advertising and trade fair participation.
- [Board depth] Independent directors include a former Executive Director of SAIL and Whole Time Director of NMDC, a retired IAS officer, and a retired SBI Chief General Manager (Lucknow Circle), alongside a promoter team led by Suresh Kumar Goyal (Chairman & MD, 25+ years).
